bullets.title: ACN: Broad earnings miss triggers -14% drop; bookings decelerate, FY26 guide cut
bullets.body: Accenture Q3 revenue of $18.72B missed consensus by ~0.3%, bookings fell 2% YoY to $19.3B (vs +7% expected), and FY26 growth guidance was cut to 3-4% cc from 3-5%. Managed Services book-to-bill fell below 1.0x for first time since 2019; MS downgraded to Equal-weight. JPM maintains Overweight, viewing the $4.175B OT cybersecurity acquisition pivot (Dragos/runZero/NetRise) as strategic rather than a sign of desperation, though the deal adds only ~0.3% to revenue.

bullets.title: INTC: +9% on Trump-Apple domestic chip manufacturing announcement
bullets.body: Trump announced Apple has agreed to work with Intel to design and build chips in America, sending INTC up ~9% pre-market. Analysts note the collaboration is not entirely new/surprising, but the political visibility accelerates sentiment. Broad semi sector strength followed with SOXX ETF +4.38%.

bullets.title: AMD: Citi upgrades to Buy with $575 PT on Meta MI450 GPU win and CPU TAM expansion
bullets.body: Citi analyst Atif Malik upgraded AMD to Buy (PT $575) citing AMD's expected win of the lion's share of Meta's custom MI450 GPU opportunity, which offers lower TCO vs. merchant products. The estimated TAM is ~$15B per gigawatt, with AMD also benefiting from higher CPU TAM expectations.

bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin marks shift to AI factory era; 800V power architecture the key gating factor
bullets.body: Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers 10x more tokens per megawatt than GB200 and 1/10th the cost per million tokens for inference; NVLink 6 provides 3.6TB/s per GPU. NVIDIA is leading the 800V DC data-center power infrastructure transition starting 2027, which reduces resistive losses by >100x vs. 54V systems and enables multi-megawatt racks. Separately, Amazon is in discussions to sell its custom AI chips to third parties, positioning as a lower-cost NVDA rival.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $50/watt GPU rental deal signals compute scarcity; bullish read for META, CRWV capex
bullets.body: Google is renting ~110K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs at ~$50/watt annually, materially above the ~$12-14/watt neocloud contract rates, signaling strong AI monetization expectations. MS raised GOOGL capex estimate to $375B by 2028. The deal is bullish for CRWV and NBIS neocloud economics and supports META's 4.4/3.9 GW incremental capacity build in '26/'27.

bullets.title: TXN: Best-positioned for 800V data center power conversion; TAM to grow 75% CAGR to $12B by 2028
bullets.body: Citi sees TXN as the primary beneficiary of the 800V DC power architecture transition in AI data centers, citing its high-voltage GaN capabilities and 300mm capacity. The 800V TAM is expected to grow from ~$2B in 2025 to $12B in 2028 at a 75% CAGR, with CSP-driven adoption beginning in 2H27.

bullets.title: MU: Memory cost crisis drives AAPL price hike plans; MU bullish into 2027-28
bullets.body: Memory BOM costs are rising 80-90% YTD and triple-digits YoY, forcing AAPL to plan iPhone/Mac/iPad price hikes of $100-200+ on iPhone 18. Hyperscalers are pre-paying and locking long-term DRAM/NAND supply, pushing AAPL to the back of the queue. UBS carries a Street-high $1,625 PT on MU with a pathway to >$100 EPS and >$400B FCF through 2029, while MS raised its CY26/CY27 MU forecasts to $12.63/$16.21.

bullets.title: META: Manus acquisition unwound after China block; exploring equity raises and external capital structures
bullets.body: China's NDRC blocked Meta's ~$2B acquisition of Manus; Meta has stopped sharing data with Manus and is sunsetting the product, with original Chinese backers (Tencent, HSG, ZhenFund) planning to re-acquire at the same price. Separately, META is exploring bond JVs, sovereign wealth participation, and potentially tens of billions in equity raises to fund its 4.4/3.9 GW AI capacity buildout in '26/'27. MS raised META capex estimate to $205B by 2028.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI pre-orders confirmed for June 25; Nov 19 launch intact; ~33M units implied by guidance
bullets.body: Rockstar confirmed GTA VI pre-orders begin June 25 across digital storefronts and select retailers, maintaining the November 19, 2026 launch date. FY27 guidance implies ~33M GTA VI first-year unit sales, conservative vs. the prior GTA title. UBS maintains Buy with a base case of $2.0B in full game sales in F27.

bullets.title: FERC unanimously approves Trump plan to accelerate AI data center grid connections
bullets.body: FERC voted unanimously to approve the Trump administration plan directing grid operators to allow large loads like AI data centers to connect in a timely and orderly manner. The ruling is a positive catalyst for power infrastructure plays including CEG, CRWV, BE, and NBIS.

bullets.title: LYV: Ticketmaster divestiture risk elevated as states pursue remedy after monopolization ruling
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes the DOJ settlement allows antitrust approval by late fall, but state AGs are actively pursuing Ticketmaster divestiture following the jury finding of illegal monopolization. Divestiture risk is characterized as significant, making this a key overhang on LYV shares.

bullets.title: TSLA: Oppenheimer raises capex estimates 25% above street on Physical AI and Terafab thesis
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raised TSLA capex guidance by $3B to $29.4B in 2026 and $3.5B to $30.4B in 2027, driven by data center and Terafab investments. The analyst's estimates are now ~25% above street consensus, with the narrative shifting toward TSLA as a vertically integrated Physical AI complex. Solar and storage ramp is seen as an underappreciated accelerant.

bullets.title: SHOP: UBS screening as clear AI beneficiary for SMB workflows; investor lunch July 15
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's SMB survey shows Shopify as a clear AI beneficiary with strong merchant intent for AI-enabled workflows. UBS is hosting a Boston investor lunch on July 15 covering Shop Campaigns, Payments GPV penetration, enterprise traction, agentic commerce, and take-rate dynamics.

bullets.title: INTU: At 52-week lows; AI accounting workflow demand is tailwind but stock -65% YoY
bullets.body: INTU is flagged at a 52-week low, down 65% YoY. Morgan Stanley's survey identifies INTU as aligned with rising AI demand in accounting/finance workflows, with intelligent risk alerts and automated bookkeeping as top enterprise use cases — though near-term stock pressure persists.

bullets.title: AMZN: Custom AI chips to be sold externally; Kyndryl expands AWS collaboration
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports Amazon is in discussions to sell its custom AI chips for data center use to third parties, positioning them as a lower-cost Nvidia alternative. Separately, Kyndryl and AWS signed an expanded strategic collaboration agreement focused on agentic AI and modernization, with over 11,000 AWS-certified Kyndryl professionals involved.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: Beneficiaries of GOOGL $50/watt GPU rental pricing and FERC grid approval
bullets.body: CoreWeave and Nebius are flagged as direct beneficiaries of Google's ~$50/watt GPU rental deal (vs. ~$12-14 standard neocloud rates), validating premium neocloud pricing power. The FERC unanimous approval of accelerated AI data center grid connections further supports both names' infrastructure buildout timelines.

bullets.title: AVGO/MRVL: Semi sector strength; MRVL plans TSMC 1.4nm for AI data center
bullets.body: Broad semiconductor sector strength driven by AI capex acceleration. MRVL plans to leverage TSMC's 1.4nm technology node for AI data center and supercomputing applications. Citi raised WFE estimates to $145B/'$200B/$250B for 2026-2028, benefiting AVGO and the broader ecosystem.

bullets.title: VZ/T/CMCSA: Telecom Big 3 down -2.6% YTD; TMUS rated Outperform at $255 (+41%)
bullets.body: Wolfe Research notes FWA availability for T-Mobile and Verizon declined -3.5% and -1.9% respectively in May, while AT&T's net adds accelerated in 1Q26. The Big 3 trade at 6.8x NTM EBITDA on average; TMUS is rated Outperform with a $255 PT (40.6% upside), while T and VZ are Peer Perform. SpaceX/Starlink is flagged as a rising sector risk.

bullets.title: CEG/VST/TLN: FERC and PUCT meetings address data center interconnection; power stocks in focus
bullets.body: FERC met at 10am ET to address data center interconnection and co-location tariffs in PJM; PUCT met to discuss ERCOT's batch interconnection process with 35 GW baseload and 65 GW under study in Batch 0. Goldman Sachs initiated TLN at Buy pre-market. The policy clarity is a positive catalyst for IPP and power infrastructure names.

bullets.title: OMC: Unusual call-skewed options activity; stock -4.9% with P/C ratio 16.79
bullets.body: StreetAccount flagged OMC with options volume 396% above 30-day average (1,370 contracts) and a heavily call-skewed put/call ratio of 16.79, despite the stock being down 4.9% on the day. The divergence between price action and options flow is notable.
